title: How Hunter Isaacson built NGL: simple, shareable apps that grow virally
summary: Hunter Isaacson traces his path from failed first app Leader to Zoom University, Nine Count and NGL (100M+ downloads). Core lessons: design apps where each user brings the next, keep products radically simple, iterate on small tweaks, and treat failure unemotionally.

principles.text: Before building an app, ask how it grows organically: person A must bring person B.
principles.quote: if you're building an app make sure you figure out how how can person a bring person B and they bring person C and so on and so forth

principles.text: Frame every app as an exchange: define what you give the user and what you get from them.
principles.quote: what am I giving what am I getting and that's really important it's something think people don't really talk about enough is is that's really what this is it's it's a it's an exchange

principles.text: Build one simple thing that meets a specific demand; don't keep adding features once it works.
principles.quote: build something that just meets this specific demand and focus on that and don't over complicate it

principles.text: Make the app a funnel to share, so growth continues as long as people keep sharing it.
principles.quote: if the whole app is just about sharing then as long as somebody shares the app it's going to keep growing

principles.text: Small, measured tweaks turned a dud into a hit: test a change, keep wins, roll back losses.
principles.quote: making a change looking at the numbers and being like okay that was a good change let's do another one oh that was a bad change roll it back

principles.text: Go cross-platform: Android drove NGL's downloads worldwide while iPhone drove revenue.
principles.quote: Android gave us the downloads iPhone gave us the revenue
